## FlushKeys
Throws away everything the keyboard has recorded so far: the queue of typed characters that [GetKey](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#getkey) hands out, the keys counted as held for [KeyDown](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#keydown) and the presses counted for [KeyHit](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#keyhit). Call it once before a screen that waits for input, such as a menu or a new level, so that button mashing from the previous screen does not skip it. Do not call it every frame, or the program will never see a key.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Text 10, 10, "Mash the keys for a moment..."
Flip
Delay 2000
FlushKeys
Cls
Text 10, 10, "Everything typed so far is forgotten."
Text 10, 30, "Press any key to leave."
Flip
WaitKey
```

## GetKey
Takes the next typed character out of the keyboard queue and returns its character code, or 0 when nothing was typed since the last call. It follows what the keyboard layout produces, so Shift+A gives 65 and plain A gives 97. A few keys that do not type a character still give a code: Enter 13, Backspace 8, Tab 9 and Escape 27, and the editing keys give the codes of the original: Home 1, End 2, Insert 3, Delete 4, Page Up 5, Page Down 6, and the arrows Up 28, Down 29, Left 30 and Right 31. Keys without any character, such as Shift and the function keys, are not reported here, so use [KeyDown](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#keydown) or [KeyHit](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#keyhit) for those.

The character code is not the scancode that KeyDown and KeyHit use.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Local typed$ = ""
While Not KeyHit(1)
	Local c = GetKey()
	If c = 8 And Len(typed) > 0 Then typed = Left(typed, Len(typed) - 1)
	If c >= 32 And c < 127 Then typed = typed + Chr(c)
	Cls
	Text 10, 10, "Type something, Escape ends:"
	Text 10, 30, typed + "_"
	Flip
Wend
```
@returns The character code of the next typed character, or 0 if there is none.
@gap The queue holds 64 characters, and the oldest ones are dropped when it is full.
@gap Only characters that fit into one byte (code 1 to 255) are delivered. Characters outside the Latin-1 range, such as many symbols typed through an IME, are skipped.

## KeyDown
Tells whether a key is held down right now. Keys are named by their scancode, which is the position of the key on the keyboard and does not change with the keyboard layout. Some of them: Escape 1, the digit row 2 to 11, Backspace 14, Tab 15, Enter 28, left Ctrl 29, left Shift 42, right Shift 54, left Alt 56, Space 57, F1 to F10 59 to 68, F11 87, F12 88, Up 200, Left 203, Right 205, Down 208, Insert 210 and Delete 211. The letter keys follow the top left to bottom right order of a US keyboard, so Q is 16, A is 30 and Z is 44.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Local x = 160, y = 120
While Not KeyDown(1)
	If KeyDown(203) Then x = x - 2
	If KeyDown(205) Then x = x + 2
	If KeyDown(200) Then y = y - 2
	If KeyDown(208) Then y = y + 2
	Cls
	Text 10, 10, "Arrow keys move the box, Escape ends"
	Rect x - 8, y - 8, 16, 16, 1
	Flip
Wend
```
@param key  The scancode of the key, 1 to 255.
@returns 1 while the key is held down, otherwise 0.
@gap Keys that have no scancode in the original table, such as Pause, Print Screen, the Windows keys and F13 and above, are never reported as pressed.
@gap Without an open graphics window nothing can be pressed, and the function returns 0.

## KeyHit
Counts how often a key was pressed since the last time KeyHit asked about that same key. The count starts again from zero on every call, so the key must be released and pressed again to count another time. This is the right choice for one-shot actions like pausing or shooting, while [KeyDown](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#keydown) suits continuous movement.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Local hits = 0
While Not KeyHit(1)
	If KeyHit(57) Then hits = hits + 1
	Cls
	Text 10, 10, "Press Space, Escape ends"
	Text 10, 30, "Space was pressed " + hits + " times"
	Flip
Wend
```
@param key  The scancode of the key, 1 to 255.
@returns How many times the key was pressed since the last call.

## WaitKey
Stops the program until a character is typed and returns its character code. The window stays responsive while it waits, and keys that were typed before the call are ignored, so it always waits for a fresh key. Like [GetKey](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#getkey) it only reacts to keys that type a character, so Shift, Ctrl and the arrow keys do not end the wait.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Text 10, 10, "Press a key"
Flip
Local c = WaitKey()
Cls
Text 10, 10, "You typed code " + c
Flip
Delay 1000
```
@returns The character code of the key that was typed.

## KeyWait
The BlitzPlus name for [WaitKey](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#waitkey). It behaves exactly the same.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Text 10, 10, "Press any character key"
Flip
KeyWait()
```
@returns The character code of the key that was typed.
